text:
katie: Quick sync — onboarding doc shows SDK raising generic RuntimeError for HTTP failures. Customers are confused.
ryan: We had a design doc for typed exceptions but parity across languages never landed. We should standardize classes: RateLimitError, AuthError, TransientError, ClientError, ConflictError.
marta: runtime: note that some 503s are permanent (model OOM) and should be surfaced as non-retryable. Need a `retryable` flag on error objects.
sanjay: security note: don't include internal traces in user-facing messages. add stable error codes (e.g. RI-ERR-XXXX) and a `safe_hint` field.
katie: Proposed SDK error payload example:
```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "RateLimitError",
    "message": "Too many requests",
    "status": 429,
    "retry_after": 2.5,
    "code": "rate_limit.exceeded"
  }
}
```
ryan: Suggest mapping table (quick): 401->AuthError (no retry), 403->AuthError (no retry), 429->RateLimitError (retry with backoff), 400->ClientError (no retry), 409->ConflictError (no retry), 500/502/503->TransientError (retryable true except when runtime marks non-retryable).
katie: Also update sample app to show catching typed exceptions and honoring `retry_after` / `retryable`.
marta: I'll add sanitized error-code emission from runtime and `safe_hint`.
leo (devx-bot): created issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4527 for tracking
ryan: follow-up: add automated parity tests per SDK to assert error classes + sampleapp coverage.
katie: I'll open docs + sampleapp PR; @ryan can own parity tests?
ryan: yep
katie: thanks :thumbsup:
